thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Roar Back After Monday's Big Reversal South

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Roar Back After Monday's Big Reversal South
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
Dow component Coca-Cola gains after topping earnings expectations; Pfizer disappoints on results
Stocks on Tuesday traded higher as President Donald Trump signaled that the U.S. is ready to reach a deal to ease trade tensions with China, giving the market much-needed relief.
However, the market remained volatile with the indexes choppy a day after the Dow Jones Industrial Average staged an ugly reversal to end the session with a triple-digit loss, partly on the back of tariff worries amid fears about global growth and peak earnings.
How are major benchmarks faring?
The Dow rose 277 points, or 1.1%, to 24,721, the S&P 500 index gained 25 points, or 0.9%, to 2,666, and the Nasdaq Composite Index climbed 63 points, or 0.9%, to 7,113.
On Monday, all main indexes finished sharply lower with the Dow swinging more than 900 points. The reversal added to the market's October woes, as the blue-chip index is down about 7% month-to-date, the S&P 500 has fallen almost 9%, while the Nasdaq is 12% in the red.
What is driving the market?
Stocks have entered a decidedly more volatile phase of trade, fueled by myriad concerns, with doubts about the health of the global economy chief among them.
Moreover, shares of companies that have done the most to help drive the U.S. stock market to repeated highs have come off the rails. So-called FAANGs, the acronym referring to technology and internet-related giants Facebook Inc. (FB), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Apple Inc. (AAPL), Netflix Inc. (NFLX) and Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL) were all trading sharply lower for October. Amazon.com on Monday fell into bear-market territory, wiping out about $120 billion in market value.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq is in correction territory, defined as a drop of at least 10% from a recent peak, while the Dow and S&P 500 are both flirting with tumbling into correction for the second time in 2018.
Comments from Trump during a Fox News interview late Monday about his readiness for a deal with China is helping to boost sentiment even though the president has not indicated that any agreement was imminent. During an interview with Laura Ingraham of Fox News, he said that the U.S. "will make a great deal with China and it has to be great, because they've drained our country."
Stock losses on Monday accelerated after a Bloomberg report indicated that White House is prepared to announce tariffs on remaining Chinese imports (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-turns-negative-amid-report-that-us-set-to-impose-tariffs-on-all-remaining-chinese-imports-2018-10-29) if talks next month between Trump and Xi Jinping don't yield results.
Markets were also digesting a raft of quarterly corporate results with several big-name companies set to report earnings after the bell, including Facebook, e-Bay Inc. (EBAY), and MGM Resorts International(MGM).
What data are in focus?
Home price gains are slowing, as the Case-Shiller 10-city composite index showed a 0.6% increase from last month's reading (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/house-price-gains-lurch-to-a-20-month-low-case-shiller-says-2018-10-30), or a 5.5% annual increase. The 20-city composite index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.1% and was 5.5% higher compared to its level a year ago, the lowest annual increase in nearly two years.
Consumer sentiment hit an 18-year high (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/americans-are-the-most-confident-in-the-economy-in-18-years-despite-stock-slump-2018-10-30), according to the Conference Board's consumer confidence index, which rose to 137.9, from 135.3 in September.
The residential vacancy rate fell 0.4 percentage points from a year earlier to 7.1%, according to the Census Bureau report, which also showed that the U.S. homeownership rate was virtually unchanged at 64.4%
What are analysts saying?
"We are seeing an oversold technical rally before we head even lower," Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA, predicted. "Most traders I talk to are still waiting for the capitulation shake off before they call a bottom."
"It may sound hard to believe, but today's positive open will be the 11th time in 22 trading days this month that equities opened the day higher," wrote Paul Hickey, co-founder of Bespoke Market Intelligence in a note to clients. "The problem, as we all know by now, is what happens once that opening bell rings; there have only been six trading days where stocks have finished the day higher than they open."
What stocks were in focus?
General Electric Co. (GE) sank 11% after it slashed its dividend (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ge-slashes-dividend-plans-to-split-up-power-unit-2018-10-30-74852749) and reported disappointing third-quarter results but announced a restructuring of its power business.
Shares of Coca-Cola Co. (KO) rose 2% after the beverage and snack giant reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that topped expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/coca-colas-stock-gains-after-earnings-and-revenue-rise-above-expectations-2018-10-30).
Pfizer Inc.'s stock (PFE) fell 1.2% after the pharmaceutical giant reported third-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pfizers-stock-falls-after-profit-beats-but-revenue-misses-2018-10-30) that beat expectations but revenue that missed, and provided a downbeat revenue outlook.
Shares of cloud services firm Akamai Technologies, Inc. (AKAM) surged 18% after the firm beat third-quarter estimates and raised its fourth-quarter guidance and full-year outlook in an earnings release Monday evening.
Under Armour Inc. (UAA) jumped 23% after the company announced third-quarter earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shares-of-under-armour-up-94-after-earnings-beat-2018-10-30) that beat analysts' estimates.
Shares in Cognizant Technology Corp. (CTSH) slid 4.3% after the technology-services firm said its profit shrank in the third-quarter, year-over-year, falling short of analysts expectations.
Masco Corp. (MAS) rallied 7.4% after missing analysts profit estimates, but surpassing revenue expectations.
KLA-Tencor Corp. (KLAC) jumped 6.8% following a third-quarter earnings release that beat Wall Street estimates.
Chesapeake Energy Corp. (CHK) skidded 13% after it announced (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chesapeake-energy-to-acquire-wildhorse-in-cash-and-stock-deal-valued-at-about-4-billion-2018-10-30) that it would acquire WildHorse Resource Development Corp. (WRD) in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $4 billion. WildHorse shares are up 5.3%.
How are other markets trading?
Asian markets finished higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-as-us-china-trade-tensions-rear-up-again-2018-10-29) but European stocks were mostly lower as the Stoxx Europe 600 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/italian-stocks-lead-europe-markets-higher-banks-auto-names-climb-2018-10-29) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/italian-stocks-lead-europe-markets-higher-banks-auto-names-climb-2018-10-29)slipped.
Oil futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-deepens-late-october-retreat-as-latest-supply-picture-looms-2018-10-30) extended their losses and gold prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-loses-ground-as-stocks-stabilize-dollar-gains-2018-10-30) settled lower, while the U.S. dollar was firmer.
--Mark DeCambre contributed to this report
